dynamic_rules.security_list_reports.r04.d01: office_scope (legacy section LOCATION): office_scope.mode = office_group switches the picker to lookup:office_groups and the selection fills office_group_id (one group) or office_group_ids (several, enhancement); mode office fills office_ids (default working_office). A group resolves to its member offices intersected with the offices the caller may read. With no office groups defined (every migrated tenant: office_groups is empty) the group mode offers the single value all, which resolves to every office the caller may read - the legacy 'group run covers all offices'. The resolved office set filters the user's office assignment (office_attribution = assigned_office, NEW, user_offices.office_id), not the security group: DentC security groups are organisation-level and carry no office. Not offered on lists.user_list, lists.group_list, lists.group_rights_list (no LOCATION control, scope.office_mode = none).

security_list_reports.r01.s02.c01.notes: Legacy SELECT dialog (dual list with INCLUDE ALL, search, sort) becomes a searchable multi-select; ALL = no restriction. Role on this report: the listed user account itself (rpt_user_dim.user_id IN (:user_ids)), not a poster or creator of records. Only real accounts are listed (rpt_user_dim rows with is_legacy_login = false); bare legacy login strings are never rows or options. The option source lookup:users returns active and inactive users with a status badge; a picked inactive user is printed only when include_inactive_users = true (inferred: the legacy precedence of the picker over the checkbox is not documented). Dialog content never captured - confirm list source and whether inactive users are listed on the live tool.

security_list_reports.r01.s03.c01.notes: false (legacy default) = users with users.is_active = true only; true = active and inactive users, with an Active column showing the state. Applied after user_ids (a picked inactive user is dropped while unticked; inferred). Inactive in DentC = the deactivated account of Security > Users (no separate deleted state for users).

security_list_reports.r04.s02.c01.notes: Row grain of the same membership population: detail = one row per office band x security group x member user; summary = one row per office band x security group with member_count = all printed members of the band and group (active members, plus inactive members when include_inactive_users = true) and inactive_member_count = its inactive part (only when include_inactive_users = true). Both layouts are INFERRED (the report is absent from every vendor source) - confirm on the live tool. No dependency on PRINT FORMAT on this report: both formats export to PDF and Excel.

security_list_reports.r04.s03.c01.notes: Legacy SELECT dialog becomes a searchable multi-select on lookup:security_groups (GET /user-groups, id and name only, needs no data class); ALL = no restriction. Filters user_group_memberships.group_id IN (:security_group_ids). Legacy groups are defined per office (the same name under several offices, vendor-documented); DentC user_groups are organisation-level (no office column), so the picker lists each group once and the office of a row comes from the member's office assignment, not from the group. Inactive groups (user_groups.is_active = false, the delete state of the Security Groups screen) are not offered and grant nothing (effective_permissions ignores them); enhancement group_status shows them. Dialog content never captured - confirm on the live tool whether the legacy list shows office-qualified group names.

security_list_reports.r04.s04.c01.notes: Deviation (model): the legacy tool presumably filters by the security group's own office (legacy groups are defined per office); DentC groups have no office, so the member's office assignment is used (office_attribution = assigned_office, NEW value for 03 5.1: user_offices.office_id) - confirm by r04 open question 2 (RPT-SLIST-09). Options and default unchanged: LOCATION is the OFFICE/GROUP section spelled differently, Office versus Office Group, see rule d01.

security_list_reports.r04.s04.c02.notes: 108 = id of the office the user was working in (vendor-documented correction: the box defaults to the session office, SELECT picks others) -> token working_office. Offices (mode office) or office groups (mode office_group); the selection becomes exactly one of office_ids / office_group_id / office_group_ids; tokens working_office, my_offices; all = every office (or group) the caller may read. On this report the office is the member's office assignment (user_offices.office_id, all assignments, not only the primary row): a user assigned to two selected offices is listed under both office bands and counted once in the grand total. Assignments are de-duplicated per (user_id, office_id) before the band join (user_offices has no unique constraint). Users with no office assignment at all (ungated: they reach every office) are listed in a trailing band 'No office assignment' (enhancement include_unassigned_users, default true, INFERRED) and the footer echoes '* Includes users with no office assignment'; the legacy handling of such users is unknown, confirm on the live tool (r04 open question 3).

security_list_reports.r04.s05.c01.notes: false (legacy default) = members whose users.is_active = true only; true = active and inactive members, with an Active column (detail) and an inactive-member count (summary). DentC keeps memberships of a deactivated user (user_group_memberships is hard-deleted only by an edit), so the checkbox decides whether those rows print.
